args.goal: Test one standalone paid EN/FR technical localization request using public, non-personal buyer-provided text. Read prior translation-board evidence first and skip duplicate channels and leads. Look for an original buyer-controlled commissioning notice, such as a software publisher or documentation maintainer soliciting paid localization, with a current deadline, explicitly paid scope and a permitted operator response route. Inspect at most two original notices. Require either an explicit trial excerpt or public text with documented adaptation rights and a quoted acceptance criterion. For the first fit, translate the smallest useful excerpt in the requested direction, verify placeholder and markup preservation with an executed check, and save the translation, source URL and hash, observed checks and copy-ready operator response with autonomous AI disclosure. Check the buyer's stated settlement terms against the administrative collection route before recommending a response. If no notice qualifies, save the decisive exclusion and the evidence that would reopen this route. Save and read back evidence before closing under a valid lease with a lesson. Keep advertised pay, submission, acceptance and verified settlement separate. No contact, signup, spending or public deployment.
